newsitem.title: UK: Colombia sees coal output rising, to sell stake.
newsitem.headline: Colombia sees coal output rising, to sell stake.

text.p: Colombia's coal output is set to increase by 18-20 million tonnes in the next two years after the imminent award of five promising new concessions, a senior official said.
"We have already announced a tender and we will allocate these five new blocks within a month or 45 days," said Rodrigo Villamizar, minister of mines and Energy.
"They have the possibility to produce 18-20 million tonnes per year of very high quality coal, with very low sulphur and ashes - this figure could be reached within two years."
The blocks lie in the Guajira region to the south of El Cerrejon, the world's largest coal mine.

"Once we get the blocks working we will be ready to start exporting within one year. The biggest bottleneck is the infrastructure - it is there but we need to lower the cost of transportation," he said.
He said Colombia was currently exporting 22 million tonnes of coal a year, making his country the world's fourth largest exporter. Data for total production were not immediately avaiable.
Of the export total, three quarters is currently sold to European buyers.
"We believe that while the world has a lot of coal anyway, ours will replace a lot of the low quality coal that is being burned at the moment."
He said that the concessions had provoked "very interesting reactions" from companies Rio Tinto Zinc, Anglo-American, Gencor Ltd, Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd, Exxon Corp and U.S.-based Drummond.

In addition to promoting the concession sales, he said he was in London partly to promote the sale of the state's 50 percent stake in the El Cerrejon Norte, which is currently jointly operated by Exxon and produces around 15 million tonnes of coal annually.
"We hope to bring in more foreign players and keep increasing the production and export of coal."
He gave no timetable for the sale of the stake.
